project: The Formula of Becoming - Week 1 Day 6 - Full Cast

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: Indigo Night transformed Hart Student Union into a festival of music, food, club tables, and first-year students trying out possible versions of themselves.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: Nia moved through it like a spark in dry grass. She signed an interest card for the Association for Women in Mathematics, took a flyer from Math Circle, promised to visit campus radio, and nearly volunteered for a service event before Malik removed the pen from her hand.

items.speaker: malik
items.text: You cannot join the whole university tonight.

items.speaker: nia
items.text: Watch me.

items.speaker: malik
items.text: I am watching. It is concerning.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: Across the terrace, an alto saxophone climbed above the crowd. A small group from the Marching Herons was performing beside the radio booth. The saxophonist played with his eyes half closed, then opened them at the exact moment Nia stepped closer.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: After the set, he introduced himself as Julian Cross, second-year media arts student, campus radio host, and, according to him,

items.speaker: julian
items.text: occasional rescuer of boring events.

items.speaker: nia
items.text: This event was not boring,

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: Nia said.

items.speaker: julian
items.text: Then I can take the night off.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: His confidence should have been irritating. Somehow, it was not.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: Julian told her about a radio showcase on Friday and invited her to stop by. Nia said yes with the speed she used for nearly every interesting opportunity.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: At another table, Malik found a sign for the Heron Analytics Challenge. Fourth-down decisions. Player performance. Ticket demand. Real datasets, competitive teams, regional presentations.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: He read every line twice before writing his name.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: When he and Nia met again near the Copper Cup Cafe, they both had news.

items.speaker: nia
items.text: I got invited to the radio showcase,

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: Nia said.

items.speaker: malik
items.text: I signed up for an analytics information session.

items.speaker: nia
items.text: Look at us choosing things.

items.speaker: malik
items.text: You chose six things.

items.speaker: nia
items.text: Seven, technically.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: He shook his head, but his attention drifted to Julian across the room. Julian saw Nia and lifted two fingers in a casual salute. She smiled back.

items.speaker: narrator
items.text: Malik did not yet have a name for the small drop inside his chest. He treated it like a number too minor to enter.
